learningObjective: Precisely define compiler-driven memory planning and buffer reuse for tensor programs and distinguish it from runtime allocation.

canonicalClaims.claim: Compiler-driven memory planning analyzes tensor lifetimes across the data-flow graph, packs non-overlapping tensors onto shared buffers, and produces a static offset-based allocation plan that the runtime executes without per-op malloc/free.
conditions: Tensor sizes and lifetimes are known at compile time (static shapes or bounded dynamic shapes).
The compiler has global visibility over the program's data-flow graph.
nonImplications: Does not imply the runtime allocator becomes unnecessary; dynamic tensors and side effects still need it.
Does not imply the plan is provably optimal — buffer packing is NP-hard.

misconceptions.claim: Memory planning is the same thing as a caching allocator (e.g., PyTorch CUDA caching allocator).
misconceptions.whyWrong: Memory planning is compile-time and produces a plan; caching allocators are runtime mechanisms that recycle freed blocks.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: TVM memory planner vs. PyTorch caching allocator

misconceptions.claim: Buffer reuse means reusing the same buffer across multiple training iterations of the same graph.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Intra-graph reuse packs non-overlapping tensors; inter-iteration reuse is a runtime property of the allocator.

misconceptions.claim: SSA renaming is what enables buffer reuse; more SSA names mean more buffers.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SSA is an IR property; buffer assignment is a physical allocation decision downstream that ignores logical name multiplicity.

misconceptions.claim: Memory planning eliminates the need for runtime allocation entirely, even under dynamic shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamic shapes may prevent static packing; the runtime allocator must still handle unknown-size tensors.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: TVM Relax dynamic shape memory planning notes

implementationFacts: XLA's BufferAssignment pass computes live ranges and assigns HLO values to buffer allocations.
TensorRT builds a static engine plan with pre-allocated workspaces.
TVM Relax has a `StaticPlanBlockMemory` pass for compile-time buffer arenas.
performanceScenarios: A pipeline with 20 intermediate tensors may pack into 3-4 arenas via lifetime analysis, saving GBs of peak memory versus per-tensor allocation.
